title: Nuclei isolation from surgically resected human hippocampus
protocol: Resect the lateral temporal cortex to expose the hippocampus after opening the temporal horn of the ventricle.
Divide the amygdalo-hippocampal sulcus and reflect the hippocampus inferiorly on its vascular pedicle until fibria and choroidal fissure are visualized.
Open the alveus just lateral to the fimbria and dissect along the hippocampal axis until arteries feeding the hippocampus are identified and sequentially divided, freeing the hippocampus en bloc.
Sever the tail of the hippocampus posterior to the lateral geniculate nucleus.
Remove an approximately 0.5 cm segment from the anterior and posterior poles of the hippocampus for processing.
Send the middle portion of the hippocampus for neuropathological analysis.
Critical: Drop anterior and posterior hippocampal specimens into separate 50 mL conical tubes containing ice-cold Neurobasal A Medium.
Place the tubes on ice and transport them back to the laboratory within 20 minutes.
Wash tissue in ice cold 1× PBS.
Dissect out approximately 25% of each specimen for RNA integrity analysis using a scalpel.
Transfer specimens into prechilled and prelabelled Eppendorf tubes.
Flash-freeze the dissected piece in liquid nitrogen.
Isolate total RNA from the dissected piece using a standard RNA isolation method.
Determine RIN values for each sample using an RNA Screen Tape Analysis system according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Label the tubes with both case identification number and date of tissue collection.
Update the tissue inventory spreadsheet accordingly.
Dissect the surgically resected hippocampal tissue into pieces smaller than ∼0.3 cm³ on a petri dish placed on ice.
Transfer the dissected tissue pieces to a Dounce homogenizer containing 2 mL of ice-cold Nuclei EZ lysis buffer.
Use pestle A for 20 strokes, followed by 20 strokes with pestle B while on ice.
Transfer the homogenate to a 15 mL conical tube.
Add 2 mL of ice-cold Nuclei EZ lysis buffer and mix by pipetting with a glass pipette.
Incubate on ice for 5 min.
Collect the nuclei by centrifugation at 500 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard supernatant.
Carefully resuspend nuclei in 4 mL of ice-cold Nuclei EZ lysis buffer.
Incubate on ice for 5 min.
Repeat the centrifugation at 500 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the nuclei in 500 μL of nuclei suspension buffer (NSB) consisting of 1× PBS, 1% BSA, and 0.2 U/μL RNAse inhibitor.
Filter the nuclei suspension using a Flowmi Cell Strainer.
If filtering is difficult due to debris, filter smaller volumes and use a new filter for every ∼100 μL volume.
Implement a sucrose gradient to obtain a cleaner nuclei suspension.
Centrifuge the sucrose gradient for 1 hour.
Remove debris using a density gradient centrifugation.
Add 500 μL of sucrose solution to a 2 mL Eppendorf tube.
Add 900 μL of sucrose solution to 500 μL of isolated nuclei in NSB.
Layer 1400 μL of nuclei suspension on top of the sucrose solution.
Centrifuge this gradient at 13,000 × g for 45 min at 4°C.
Carefully remove the myelin layer from the top.
Remove the supernatant containing cellular debris.
Resuspend the nuclei pellet in 500 μL NSB and transfer to a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Centrifuge at 500 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 100–300 μL NSB.
Filter the suspension through a 40-μm Flowmi Cell Strainer.
Stain 10 μL of nuclei suspension with 4 μM Ethidium Homodimer-1.
Visualize stained nuclei under an epifluorescence microscope in the red channel.
Stain 10 μL of nuclei suspension with 10 μL of premade 0.4% Trypan Blue.
Load the stained sample on a hemocytometer.
Visualize the nuclei under a bright field microscope.
Count blue/purple stained nuclei.
Adjust the final concentration of nuclei to 1000 nuclei/μL with NSB.
Continue with preparation of droplet-based single-nuclei RNA-seq libraries using the Chromium Single Cell 3′ kit (10× Genomics) according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
